title: Janus-Q: End-to-End Event-Driven Trading via Hierarchical-Gated Reward Modeling
central_strategy: An unnamed language-model checkpoint is supervised and then GRPO-tuned with the Hierarchical Gated Reward Model to map each point-in-time financial-news event into event type, predicted CAR, direction, and strong/weak execution. Strong positive or negative decisions become event-weighted trades entered at the next open and exited at a subsequent two-day close.

required_but_missing: The named base model, immutable checkpoint, tokenizer, SFT output, and GRPO output.
Executable prompt parsing, prediction, reward, event aggregation, portfolio, and backtest code.
Selected reward constants and weights, inference decoding, seeds, and model responses.
Point-in-time U.S. news events aligned to the JKP top-1,000 formation universe.
An event-overlap/conflict rule, capital budget, leverage, fills, costs, and missing-price policy.
monthly_jkp_assessment.why_released_labels_are_not_a_strategy: Released direction and strength labels are deterministic functions of realized future CAR. Treating them as actions on JKP would use future returns and create direct lookahead.
monthly_jkp_assessment.why_numeric_proxy_is_not_defensible: JKP contains monthly security characteristics and returns but no news text, event taxonomy, predicted CAR, or learned event policy. A generic momentum, sentiment, or event-type factor would replace rather than preserve Janus-Q's central mechanism.
monthly_jkp_assessment.bounded_alternative_checked: The author-linked event dataset can validate label arithmetic and static NAV consistency, but it is China-specific historical output and cannot generate causal monthly U.S. decisions without a released model or a new text dataset/training project.

closure_rule: Do not train an unrelated classifier, replay future-CAR labels, substitute static author NAVs, or attribute a generic JKP factor to Janus-Q. Reopen only if a transferable checkpoint/inference policy or complete causal decision code becomes available.
